extracted.intended_audience: Australian government policy makers and policy drafters (federal and national/State bodies)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing Impact Analysis for Australian Government policy proposals, including what impacts to consider, evidence expectations, and procedural steps for engaging the Office of Impact Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider effects on people, businesses and community
rubrics_metrics.description: Help policy makers reflect on how policy can affect people, businesses and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing a proposal, identify and describe who will be affected (individuals, businesses, community organisations) and how; consider distributional as well as aggregate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider broader economic and competition impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on the proposal's broader economic and competition impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess economy-wide effects and any competition consequences that could arise from the policy, beyond direct beneficiaries or costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure costs and benefits are understood from all angles
rubrics_metrics.description: The government’s rigorous approach to policy making seeks to ensure that the costs and benefits of new policy are understood from all angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify, quantify (where possible), and explain both costs and benefits; consider short- and long-term impacts and non-monetary effects so decision makers can weigh trade-offs comprehensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a necessary evidence base to decision makers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Impact Analysis framework will ensure decision makers are provided with the necessary evidence base to make the decisions that will best support a stronger economy and guarantee the essentials Australians rely on to prosper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground assessments in up-to-date evidence, data and analysis; document methods, sources, assumptions and uncertainties so decision makers can judge reliability and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design policy options to be well‑designed, well‑targeted and fit‑for‑purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy options should be well-designed, well-targeted and fit-for-purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting options, explain rationale, intended targets, expected outcomes and why the option is appropriate compared to alternatives; consider implementation feasibility and unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply strong evidence‑based impact analysis intentionally and consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong evidence-based impact analysis is a powerful tool when applied intentionally and consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a consistent framework and standards across proposals so assessments are comparable; explicitly apply evidence standards and justify analytical choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Australian Government Policy Impact Analysis Guide / Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Access the Guide (Australian Government Guide to Policy Impact Analysis) to follow the government’s Policy Impact Analysis Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Guide's recommended steps, templates and expectations when preparing impact analyses; use provided resources (e.g., 'Impact Analysis 101' videos) for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit a Preliminary Assessment or New Policy Proposal to OIA to determine IA requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To get started, send a completed Preliminary Assessment form, or a copy of your New Policy Proposal, to helpdesk-OIA@pmc.gov.au. Once reviewed, the OIA will advise whether an Impact Analysis (IA) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage OIA early via the Preliminary Assessment process to clarify scope and whether a full IA is necessary; use OIA feedback to shape analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow updated RIAG procedures for Ministers' Meetings and national standard setting bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: National Cabinet has refocused Impact Analysis requirements for decisions in the Federal Relations Architecture: proposals in these fora are no longer required to be finalised with the OIA unless an Impact Analysis is requested by the relevant decision maker(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the updated Regulatory Impact Analysis Guide (RIAG) procedures and consult OIA about how these changes affect obligations and submission processes for intergovernmental decisions.
